answer.rationale: The low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the 18% mandate, so the cheapest path is to switch primary. Memory c2 supports that the move cut unit cost sharply and invoicing stayed accurate. Memory c4 is read as a cautionary frame: switching is fine when price is the lever, but if the low-cost vendor won't move on payment terms I'll have a narrow opening to revisit and renegotiate. Memory c3 (dual-sourcing) is relevant as a contingency because the line runs at 94% with no buffer and delivery risk cannot rise. I won't add a second source this cycle because I only have capacity for one decision; instead I will request that the new vendor hold safety stock or commit to short lead times, and keep the incumbent warm as a fallback. Service scope won't narrow because the new vendor's quote meets the mandate on price alone.
